info.title: MowBot API
info.description: API of the MowBot hub. Every client (web, mobile, desktop) uses it.

post.description: Creates the owner account. Requires the setup token printed in the hub logs.
Rotates the refresh token. Native clients send it in the body; web clients send `{}` and rely on the cookie.
Revokes the calling device.

patch.description: Name and language of the owner (bots answer in that language).

put.description: This device's push notifications: its Expo push token (null turns them off) and what it wants to hear about.

post.description: Creates a team with its own workspace and shared PC (started on first use).

delete.description: Deletes a team without bots: its PC is removed, its files move to the main team's trash.

post.description: Starts the computer in the background (status `starting`).
Stops the container. Files and home directory are kept.
Stops then starts the computer.
Gives the calling device the mouse and keyboard; bots' input is paused.

delete.description: Hands the desktop back to the bots.

post.description: One-time ticket for `GET /computers/{id}/desktop?ticket=…` (WebSocket, RFB).

delete.description: Moves to `.trash/`. Deleting inside `.trash/` removes the file for good.

get.description: Files and folders whose path contains `q` (names starting with it first); without `q`, the files changed last.
Raw bytes for previews (supports Range). Active types (HTML, scripts) are served as text.

post.description: One-time link `GET /downloads/{ticket}`: the file itself, or a zip when the path is a folder.
multipart/form-data, one or more `file` parts, stored in the `path` folder. Existing names get a ` (n)` suffix.
Renames or moves a file or folder. Fails if the target exists.
One-time ticket for the `GET /events?ticket=…` WebSocket stream.
Adds an LLM endpoint. The API key is sealed at rest and never returned. The first provider is assigned to the bots without one.

get.description: Models advertised by the endpoint. Doubles as a connection test.

post.description: Creates a bot in a team (on the team's PC or a dedicated one) or solo (own PC and workspace).

delete.description: Deletes a bot (not the Chef) and its conversation. A dedicated PC goes with it; a solo bot's files move to the main team's trash.

patch.description: Identity, mission, models (main, fallbacks, light model for check-ins), check-in rhythm and daily token budget of a bot.

get.description: Conversation with the bot, newest page first (items are oldest → newest).

post.description: Posts a message to the bot. Its answer streams through `message.delta` / `message.updated` events.

delete.description: Starts the conversation over: stops the bot, deletes its messages and closes what it left open on its computer. Workspace files are kept.

post.description: Presses a button of a card the bot showed in that message: its reply reaches the bot as your answer (once per card). Buttons that only open a link are opened by the app itself.
Answers a vault request the bot showed in that message: the values go straight into the vault (the bot only learns the reference), or `declined: true`.
Interrupts the bot's current run.
Moves a bot to another team (teamId null: solo), on the team's PC or a dedicated one. The bot stops, tidies its old computer up, and its folder follows it to the new workspace. Not the Chef.

get.description: What the bot's own Chrome window shows now (a JPEG capture), for a live view. Poll it.

post.description: Puts the bot's Chrome window in front on its computer's screen, e.g. before taking over.

get.description: Most recently updated first (200 at most).

post.description: Gives a task to a bot, which is woken up to do it.

patch.description: A status change is reported to the bot doing the task.

post.description: Empties the activity tab: deletes finished and cancelled tasks, and starts the feed over (the messages stay in the bots’ conversations).

get.description: What bots write to each other, newest page first (items oldest → newest).
Newest first: the open ones by default.

post.description: Answers with one of the suggested answers or your own words. The bot receives it as a message from you and picks up from there.
Stores a login (username, password, 2FA seed) or a secret.

patch.description: Changes labels and policy; replaces values when given (null removes a login field).

get.description: History of the entry, newest first: captures, uses, requests, decisions.

delete.description: Takes back the permission given to a bot for an `ask` entry.

post.description: Saves (or refreshes) a site's session from a running computer's Chrome: its cookies and the local storage of its open pages.

get.description: Sites with cookies in a running computer's Chrome, to pick a session to save.

post.description: Adds a server. Its tools are listed in the background (follow `mcp.updated`); an OAuth server first needs `oauth/start`.
Connects again and lists the tools (a local server starts on a bot’s computer).
Starts signing in to the server: open `authorizationUrl` in the browser; it comes back to `<redirectBase>/api/v1/mcp/oauth/callback`.

get.description: The latest calls bots made to this server, newest first.

post.description: Links a desktop app: the token, shown only here, lets it connect to `GET /connectors/ws`.

delete.description: Unlinks a computer: its token stops working and its projects go.

patch.description: Who may work in the project and how: `ask` (each command approved) or `auto`. Folders are shared from the desktop app.

delete.description: Check-ins are stopped from the bot (heartbeatMinutes: null).

post.description: Fires the routine now, even when paused, over budget or in quiet hours.
Fires a webhook routine; the request body (JSON or text, 8 KB kept) is handed to the bot as data.

get.description: The latest 100, newest first; `unread` leaves out digest-level ones.

patch.description: Pausing stops every bot at once; bots then only answer the user until resumed.

get.description: Bots' scripts the hub runs on their computers at a steady pace (no model involved): active, paused, and those stopped in the last day.
In the user’s order, hidden ones included (flagged).

patch.description: Size, visibility and folding; the content belongs to the bot.

post.description: Presses a button of a card pinned on the home page: its reply reaches the bot that pinned it.
